cuts.raw_narration: The video opens in a dark subterranean cavern deep inside the Chimera Ant nest. A pale, cat-like figure with white wavy hair, cat ears and a long white tail — wearing a dark blue double-breasted jacket — kneels before an unseen presence, then turns to camera. Red slit-pupil eyes, an unsettling wide-eyed smile. A voice-over announces the name: 'It's Neferpitou. That is the name the Queen bestowed upon me. From now on, you can call me Neferpitou.' The character is introduced as a newly-anointed lieutenant of the Chimera Ant Queen.

Elsewhere, in a moonlit forest far above the nest, the tall hunter Kite — long white hair under a blue cap, blue sash over a white shirt — stands with two boys, Gon and Killua, facing him in the dark. He speaks plainly, and he is not warm about it: he has no intention of training them on this journey, there is no time. He only brought them because he thought they might be useful. From here on, it comes down to their resolve — if it is strong, they'll develop their Nen and improve through combat; if it is weak, the ants will eat them and they will die. Hunters, he tells them, stay on the hunt no matter what. A hunt is a battle of resolve, and to be a successful hunter you must understand your enemy as well as yourself. The boys listen in silence, faces tight.

Later, back inside the Chimera Ant nest, Neferpitou stops mid-step and turns toward the camera, glowing orange cat-eyes narrowing — someone out there has just been noticed. Cut to the forest: Kite freezes mid-walk, a violet-pink aura washing across his face as he starts to sweat, then crouches low on a hilltop in a defensive stance. Gon and Killua come up behind him, alarmed. Kite turns and speaks to them with a tense, warning expression as a massive feline eye looms in the sky behind him — the visual signature of Neferpitou's En sweeping over them from miles away. The camera cuts to Neferpitou perched on a distant cliff, grinning wide, and then, softly: 'Found you.'

What follows is the fight the boys are not ready for. In a rain-soaked forest, Killua tears through the trees with an unconscious Gon slung across his back, teeth clenched, rain and tears mixing on his face. Desaturated flashes cut in — Neferpitou lunging at Kite, a slash, Kite's arm reaching up as light bursts around him — intercut with Gon's furious open-mouthed scream and Killua's terrified wide-eyed reaction in the moment of retreat. In voice-over Killua accepts the verdict: they were both worth less than a one-armed Kite. That's the reality. If Kite had been alone, this probably wouldn't have happened.

By the time Gon wakes up, they are in a quiet indoor room — Gon sitting up under a blue blanket, Killua at the edge of the bed with his head down in shadow. Gon says, plainly, that he left Kite back there to die. Killua tells him Kite is still alive — he would never be beaten by something like that — but he did get injured, and in that shape he is hiding, waiting for them to come back. So now, they get strong, and they find him. They are going to go save Kite. Gon looks at Killua with a bright, steady smile; Killua's wide blue eyes soften, wet, and he glances away, gently overwhelmed.

The final beat cuts away from the boys entirely. In a bright, quiet clearing by a glowing turquoise stream, Neferpitou sits under a tree, long silver-grey hair trailing into the water, and calmly strokes what is cradled in their lap. The camera pulls back to show what is being petted — Kite's severed head. Neferpitou smiles down at it, serene, as the scene holds and fades.
